title: Reduce GPU workspace and peak memory: activation checkpointing, scratch buffer pool, and arena tuning
author: Ava Chen
ci_history:
2026-02-19: CI run #1 — unit tests + lint — failed (flaky kernel test)
2026-02-20: CI run #2 — fixed kernel ordering + rebase — passed
2026-02-24: Integration GPU canary — passed on p4d and a100; perf harness comparisons completed
description:
Motivation: Peak GPU memory and temporary workspace usage for large sequence inference is a recurring constraint for Dedicated/Private customers. This PR applies multiple coordinated changes to reduce per-request workspace and overall activation residency so that the serving runtime can sustain higher parallelism with the same reserved capacity.

Summary of changes: activation checkpointing: add an optional, per-model checkpointing policy that checkpoints activations for transformer blocks during forward passes and recomputes them on backward/attention reuse paths where acceptable. The default is conservative (disabled for tiny models) and enabled for large models in the model catalog via verification profiles.

Scratch buffer pool & arena tuning: replace ad-hoc cudaMalloc/cudaFree transient allocations with a bounded scratch buffer pool backed by a GPU memory arena. The arena uses size-classed buckets and a short-lived eviction policy tuned for our kernel footprint to avoid fragmentation and reduce peak workspace by reusing buffers across kernels and requests. Tuned default arena sizes and max-resident thresholds based on p4d and a100 measurements.

Kernel selection & scheduling: extend the kernel selector to expose 'workspace' cost estimates and prefer lower-workspace kernels for mixed-priority scheduling. The request scheduler now has a memory-aware placement policy that biases routing toward low-workspace kernels when total resident memory is near the SLO threshold.

Continuous batching changes: implement incremental chunking for continuous batching so that large batches are split into memory-fitting chunks that stream outputs as they finish, rather than allocating workspace for the whole logical batch. This reduces instantaneous workspace requirements while preserving throughput and latency SLOs for tail cases.

KV cache & prefix caching: introduce a small LRU spool for KV cache slices so long-running contexts can spill rarely-used prefixes to host pinned memory and bring them back on demand. This reduces peak GPU usage for serving very long contexts and when many warm requests are held.

Testing and results: benchmarked on Llama-2-13B and a 7B code model across 512/1024 seq lengths on p4d and a100. Observed reductions in peak GPU memory: ~18% (13B, 512), ~25% (13B, 1024) and ~12-20% for the 7B model depending on workload mix. End-to-end throughput improved by 5-12% for high-concurrency scenarios due to lower OOM backpressure and better packing.

Compatibility and rollout: changes are opt-in via model config flags. New default arena sizes and kernel workspace estimates are applied to models in the verified catalog after dry-run validation. No public API changes.

Notes: this PR bundles multiple coordinated changes because the full benefit requires all pieces (checkpointing, arena, scheduler, batching) to interoperate. Each part can be toggled independently for troubleshooting.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Can you explain how the checkpointing policy interacts with KV cache reads? I want to ensure recompute doesn't re-read spilled KV slices unnecessarily — Ava: checkpointing is only applied to compute activations inside transformer blocks; KV cache paths are unchanged, and the spool brings back KV slices before recompute if needed (see KV spool logic).

Priya Kapoor: The arena defaults look aggressive for <8GB cards; can we gate those by instance-type? — Ava: yes, arena tuning is gated by the hardware profile; fallbacks keep older allocation path for small GPUs.

Samir Patel: Observed a flaky fused-kernel test; was this caused by the new pooling? — Ava: yes, race on buffer reuse in the pool. I added a short lifetime fence and deterministic test seed; CI re-run passed.

Marco Ruiz: Please add a regression test for continuous-batcher chunking when batch_size > max_chunk to ensure progress — Ava: added tests/integration/gpu_memory_smoke.cc and bench harness to exercise chunking under stress.
release_notes: Runtime: reduce peak GPU memory and workspace via activation checkpointing (opt-in per model)
Runtime: introduce scratch buffer pool and GPU arena to reduce fragmentation and transient allocations
Runtime: memory-aware scheduler and kernel workspace cost for safer packing
Continuous batching: chunking to reduce instantaneous workspace for large logical batches
KV cache: small spool to spill rarely-used KV slices to host memory
